items.title: OpenAI shares AI-generated proof resolving the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, demonstrating finite-time singularity formation in fluid dynamics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI has released a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, using an internal AI model more advanced than GPT-6 Astra. The proof shows that smooth three-dimensional fluid motion can develop a singularity in finite time, resolving a question that has remained open for nearly 90 years. The solution involves a vortex that spirals inward and elongates, causing fluid velocity to grow without bound while keeping energy finite, consistent with physical laws. OpenAI's system produced both an analytical proof and a formal verification in Lean, demonstrating that the Navier-Stokes equations can break down despite viscosity smoothing effects. This breakthrough was achieved through a coordinated effort of around 10,000 AI agents with access to computational tools and internet data.

items.title: Meta launches Muse, a personal AI agent for individual users
items.content_text: Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent designed to assist individual users with various tasks. The new AI agent aims to provide personalized support and enhance user productivity through advanced AI capabilities. Muse represents Meta's latest effort to integrate AI more deeply into everyday digital experiences.

items.title: GitHub project 'i-have-adhd' offers a coding assistant skill that prioritizes direct answers with numbered steps and clear next actions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The 'i-have-adhd' skill, available on GitHub, modifies coding assistants to provide ADHD-friendly outputs by leading with the next action, numbering steps, and avoiding unnecessary preamble or tangents. It aims to prevent assistants from burying answers in lengthy explanations, instead delivering concise, actionable instructions. The skill enforces rules such as specific time estimates, limiting lists to five items, and making progress visible, improving clarity and efficiency in coding help. Users can install and customize the skill via provided instructions, and it is loosely based on principles from The Adult ADHD Tool Kit adapted for AI responses.

items.title: Terence Tao warns AI is non-renewably mining open mathematical problems, risking depletion of unsolved challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Mathematician Terence Tao has expressed concern that artificial intelligence systems are rapidly solving open math problems, effectively 'non-renewably mining' these challenges. This accelerated problem-solving could exhaust the pool of unsolved mathematical questions available for future research. Tao's observation highlights potential long-term impacts of AI on the field of mathematics and the nature of mathematical discovery.

items.title: US agencies accuse Chinese AI firms of systematic industrial-scale distillation of US frontier AI models since 2024 [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: The US government, through a joint advisory from the NSA, CISA, and FBI, accuses Chinese AI companies including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba of systematically extracting proprietary capabilities from US AI models like Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and xAI's Grok since 2024. These efforts reportedly involve billions of tokens and millions of queries to distill knowledge and improve domestic AI models, forming a core part of China's AI industrial policy. The advisory details sophisticated tactics used by these companies to evade detection, such as spreading requests across multiple accounts and platforms, using proxies, and leveraging third-party services to obscure metadata. The US agencies call for coordinated responses across government, industry, and allied nations to address this large-scale distillation activity. This accusation follows longstanding concerns about Chinese economic espionage and recent similar claims regarding Moonshot AI's practices.

The campaigns involve systematic attempts to reverse-engineer or distill proprietary AI models and techniques from U.S. companies, raising concerns about intellectual property and national security implications. The report highlights the ongoing challenges in protecting AI advancements amid global competition.

items.title: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome Atlas predicting molecular effects of 9 billion possible single-letter DNA variants across the human genome
items.content_text: DeepMind has released the AlphaGenome Atlas, a comprehensive predictive map detailing the molecular impact of every possible single-letter DNA change in the human genome, covering approximately 9 billion variants. This resource aims to enhance understanding of genetic variation and its effects at a molecular level, potentially aiding research in genetics and disease.

items.title: MIT researcher uses GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex to autonomously run and calibrate superconducting qubit experiments, streamlining quantum computing workflows [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: MIT graduate student Beatriz Yankelevich connected GPT-5.6 Sol, powered by Codex, to laboratory software to automate routine measurements and calibrations on superconducting qubit chips. This AI-driven approach allowed the system to run experiments, analyze data, and adjust parameters with minimal human intervention, significantly reducing the time required for qubit characterization. The AI agent managed interdependent measurements on a six-qubit chip, identifying resonance frequencies and calibrating control pulses while adapting to signal quality. Although it struggled with noisy or ambiguous data, the system effectively handled clear experimental workflows, enabling researchers to focus on experiment design and data analysis. The MIT group now regularly employs AI agents to conduct routine quantum chip measurements, improving efficiency in their research process.

items.title: OpenAI's AI agents solve Navier-Stokes singularity problem, one of the $1 million Millennium Prize Problems, with formal verification in Lean [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI announced that a team of 10,000 autonomous AI agents solved the Navier-Stokes singularity problem, one of the six remaining Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, with their proof formally verified in the Lean programming language. This problem involves understanding whether solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid dynamics, can develop singularities where fluid velocity becomes infinite. The AI-driven solution builds on recent advances by mathematicians and researchers who developed new strategies for tackling the problem, marking a significant milestone in applying artificial intelligence to complex mathematical challenges. While the result is primarily theoretical, it deepens understanding of fluid behavior and turbulence, and may influence future mathematical and scientific research.

items.title: Anthropic warns Claude subscribers of token theft via compromised session keys and infostealer malware [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic has alerted users of its Claude AI service that hackers are stealing tokens by accessing compromised session keys, leading to unauthorized usage and billing. Affected subscribers reported unexplained token consumption despite inactivity, with some accounts auto-upgraded or drained rapidly without user action. The company identified that infostealer malware, which can capture saved passwords and session data from users' computers, is being used to hijack Claude login sessions. Anthropic has responded by suspending affected accounts, invalidating tokens, issuing refunds, and advising users to check for malware, though it did not specify how the credentials were initially compromised. One user, Grant De Swardt, experienced significant disruption and canceled his subscription due to lack of detailed usage tracking and slow support. Anthropic declined to comment on tools for users to detect misuse, highlighting ongoing challenges in protecting accounts from such attacks.

items.title: Cognition raises $2 billion at $48 billion valuation, signaling investor confidence in multiple AI coding leaders
items.content_text: Cognition, the startup behind the coding assistant Devin, announced a $2 billion funding round at a $48 billion valuation, led by Andreessen Horowitz and other major investors. This valuation comes just four months after a $26 billion valuation and reflects strong growth, with annualized run-rate revenue rising from $492 million to $900 million since May. The funding round suggests that venture capitalists believe the AI coding market can support multiple significant players rather than a winner-take-all scenario. Cognition competes with Cursor, which was valued at $50 billion before its acquisition by SpaceX, and currently commands a higher revenue multiple despite lower revenue. The company leases expensive Nvidia server clusters and is developing its own AI models to reduce reliance on third-party providers, aiming to reach $4 billion to $5 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026. Cognition counts major enterprises like Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi among its customers.

items.title: Inpaint launches Linux desktop image editor with local AI for object removal, face replacement, restoration, and upscaling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Inpaint is a new Linux-only desktop image editor that integrates local AI models for advanced editing tasks such as object removal, face replacement, image restoration, upscaling, and background manipulation. The application processes images entirely on the user's computer, enhancing privacy by avoiding cloud services, and supports common formats like PNG, JPEG, and WebP. The tool features a folder browser, mask painting, multiple inpainting models, face restoration with GFPGAN, upscaling with RealESRGAN, and background removal with edge refinement. It maintains loaded AI models in memory for efficient editing workflows and supports batch processing, export options, and a visual edit history. The application is distributed as an AppImage for portable deployment on x86-64 Linux systems and requires initial internet access to download dependencies and model weights.

items.title: Harness Engineering Papers Collection compiles research on AI model harnesses from 2019 to 2026, detailing evolution from basic loops to self-modifying code [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Harness Engineering Papers Collection gathers key research papers tracing the development of AI model harnesses, which connect model weights to external tools, contexts, and sub-agents. It covers advancements from the initial simple sampling loops in 2019 to complex harnesses capable of rewriting themselves by 2026, illustrating how surrounding code and context can dramatically affect model performance. The collection includes foundational works such as the V0 harness baseline, few-shot learning techniques, chain-of-thought prompting, and later innovations that expand the harness's action space to include web browsing, tool use, self-critique, and recursion. This progression highlights how harness design has evolved to enhance AI capabilities by integrating external actions and dynamic code modifications.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra expands AI capabilities for individuals and businesses, enabling more affordable and complex work across consumer and enterprise sectors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI highlights how its GPT-6 Astra model advances AI intelligence and alignment, broadening the range of tasks people and businesses can perform more efficiently and affordably. The company emphasizes its integrated approach combining research, product deployment, and compute infrastructure to deliver these capabilities to over one billion weekly users and 2.5 million businesses. The article details how increased AI capability and efficiency enable new markets and workflows, citing examples such as AI-assisted medical diagnoses, software development, customer service automation, and economic analysis. OpenAI also notes that user engagement grows over time, supporting a business model that includes free access, subscriptions, and usage-based offerings. The company expects continued expansion of AI-driven work and innovation across personal and professional contexts.

items.title: Microsoft patches a record 972 vulnerabilities in September update, including 112 critical flaws amid rising AI-assisted attack threats [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Microsoft released its September patch fixing approximately 972 vulnerabilities, 112 of which are critical, marking a record high following previous months with fewer patches. This surge in patches comes as the industry braces for an increase in AI-assisted cyberattacks, with major companies warning of a narrowing window to address vulnerabilities before exploitation. Notable fixes include two zero-day vulnerabilities in Windows components, a remote code execution flaw in Exchange Server triggered by malicious email attachments, and multiple privilege escalation issues in Microsoft Authenticator and SQL Server. Security researchers note a significant number of wormable vulnerabilities that can spread without user interaction, raising concerns about potential widespread exploitation. Experts describe this spike in vulnerability discovery and patching as the "new normal," driven by AI-assisted tools that accelerate bug detection. While some question the cost and accuracy of AI-based vulnerability hunting, the volume and severity of bugs found suggest a shift in cybersecurity dynamics, with long-term effectiveness of these methods still to be determined.

items.title: Latitude launches tools to manage and monitor growing fleets of AI agents across multiple client deployments [ * ] [ ◼ ]

The system organizes conversations, flags failures automatically through deterministic and AI-driven checks, and integrates client feedback into a unified review process. This approach aims to scale from managing a handful of agents to dozens without overwhelming support teams with scattered reports. Latitude's example setup includes multiple client deployments and development projects, demonstrating how to maintain oversight and streamline investigations across a fleet of AI agents.

items.title: OpenAI announces solution to 90-year-old Navier-Stokes problem using advanced AI model amid controversy over data access [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI claims to have solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a major unsolved mathematical challenge related to fluid dynamics, using an internal AI model more powerful than GPT-6 Astra. The company began training this model in late August and announced the breakthrough in a blog post, highlighting its significance for the mathematics community and noting it will not pursue the $1 million Millennium Prize. The announcement sparked controversy after New York University professor Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge published related findings a day earlier and raised concerns that OpenAI may have accessed their Codex data during training. OpenAI denied accessing specific user data but acknowledged that de-identified data might have contributed to model improvements. Both parties maintain their proofs differ significantly, and the dispute highlights tensions around AI-assisted mathematical research and data usage.

items.title: Analysis of common misconceptions about AI replacing jobs, highlighting differences in human and AI roles across programming, art, and mathematics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The article critiques popular arguments about AI's impact on employment, emphasizing that AI does not simply replace human jobs but changes the nature of work in fields like programming, art, and mathematics. It uses examples such as chess and calculators to illustrate that human engagement often persists despite AI advancements because of different underlying values and purposes. It further discusses how AI automation may affect jobs in stages, starting with simpler tasks like web development and potentially advancing to complex fields like AI research. The author expresses concern about a future where superintelligent AI could make human problem-solving obsolete, underscoring the emotional and existential implications beyond economic factors.

items.title: NeurIPS desk-rejected 178 papers for being "AI-generated". The detector flagged the track chairs' own papers at 24-69% [N] [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: hey all. the NeurIPS Position Paper Track just used a proprietary AI detector (Pangram) to desk-reject 18.4% of all submissions. no human review, no appeal process, just out. there's been a lot of noise about this, so i went through the actual conference statements and Pangram's technical docs to see how this actually went down. the reality is wildly worse than just "the AI detector made a mistake." here are the receipts: The track chairs would have failed their own test. Independent researchers ran recent papers authored by the three track chairs through the exact same detector. It flagged them at 24% to 69%. Under their own enforcement rules, the chairs would have been at risk of rejection themselves. The detector originally flagged 42.7% of the entire track. Pangram's default setting flagged nearly half of all submissions as 90-100% AI. They had to frantically shrink the text windows just to get the flag rate down to a somewhat believable 12.7%. The "Circularity Trap". 22 papers were rejected specifically because they scored >0.5 on the detector, but the authors checked a box denying AI use. The black-box score was literally used as proof the author was lying. The massive ESL penalty. A stanford study showed 61.22% of human-written TOEFL essays get falsely flagged as AI because non-native formal English is structurally rigid. NeurIPS published zero demographic calibration data for this. If you're an ESL researcher, you were basically playing Russian roulette. if you were one of the 178 rejected: there is no blacklist. this is not a misconduct mark on your record. just take your paper and resubmit it to ICLR (deadline sept 25) or ICML. wrote up a full Field Note with the exact thresholds, the data privacy issues, and the actual recourse options if you want the hard numbers instead of just vibes: https://strictcite.com/blog/neurips-2026-position-paper-pangram-ai-detection (disclosure since it's relevant: i built strictcite.com, a deterministic zero-AI citation checker. watching a major conference use a black-box AI to nuke 178 papers with zero appeal is exactly why i hate relying on AI for this stuff. not trying to sneak the link in, just being upfront about who i am.) submitted by /u/tughanbulut [link] [comments]
